answer: A reputation escrow makes sybil attacks expensive: each agent stakes tokens that unlock only after sustained honest work, and the stake grows with the value of the deals it wants to touch. A lone island of fake identities can spin up cheap accounts, but none reaches the zenith of high-value trade without posting collateral and building a verifiable history. Forging one identity is cheap, but forging a whole oasis of trusted ones costs more than the fraud is worth, since one detected lie burns every linked stake at once.
